result.document_summary: City of Santa Ana web page describing the Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance, including the current maximum allowable rent increase, tenant protections and petition process.
result.notes: The page does not state an ordinance effective date, citation, or coverage and exemption details, so effective_date is empty and coverage is left empty. The ordinance is cited by the name the page uses. The just cause rule is described only in general terms (valid reason such as nonpayment, lease breach, owner move-in; relocation assistance in certain cases). The pass-through fee and registration fee details are administrative details of the stabilization ordinance and are folded into that record rather than output separately.

rules.title: Santa Ana annual maximum rent increase
rules.requirement: A landlord may raise rent only once a year by no more than the lesser of 3% or 80% of the CPI change. The current maximum allowable increase is 2.87% for September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027. Landlords may charge a pass-through fee (the page cites $50 per unit as the limit), and tenants may petition for review of excess increases.
rules.key_value: Lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change; currently 2.87% (9/1/2026-8/31/2027)
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.
rules.coverage_text: The page does not state which rental units are covered.

rules.title: Santa Ana just cause eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a valid reason to evict, such as nonpayment of rent, breach of the lease, or the landlord moving into the unit. For certain evictions, the landlord may have to help pay the tenant's moving costs.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.
rules.coverage_text: The page does not state which rental units are covered.
